contribution: Test whether a fixed spatial memory budget benefits from retaining complementary early-feature evidence resembling an automatic prompt's target, distant context and prompt-boundary band. Selection occurs across previously compressed Lean memory entries, allowing parts of more prior frames to survive. This is a new training-free hypothesis, not Cutie or FBB-HFNet and not a trained attention module.
reference: The original one-time automatic YOLO/SAM prompt supplies the mask. Existing early-FPN foreground/background prototypes and their contrast are reused. A third prototype is the mean initial early-FPN feature weighted by a two-cell morphological band around that prompt; each subsequent source frame is scored by cosine similarity to that fixed prototype and area-mapped onto the original 64x64 memory grid. Similar appearance is not proof that a source token lies on the true boundary. No ground-truth input, re-detection, new confidence gate or decision threshold.
selection: Reuse the author's 1024 selected tokens per compressed frame and frozen source-local usage ranks. For each fixed-capacity admission, allocate disjoint thirds to usage plus foreground contrast, usage plus background contrast, and usage plus boundary-prototype similarity, with deterministic ties and exact quota fill. Preserve feature, position, ID and score alignment; do not change model weights, automatic prompt schedule, insurance bank or protected condition/newest 4096-token memories. Dropped tokens cannot be recovered.
controls: At identical capacity and inputs use existing usage-only, foreground/background contrast and spatially distributed selection. Before any full-video experiment use separately captured same-state inputs with matched-size token interventions and unchanged conditioning/newest memories, plus foreground-only, shuffled and RGB controls where implementable. Fixed role allocation and source-local usage ranks are hypotheses, not measures of causal utility.
budget: 16384 represented spatial feature tokens including a fixed 3072 insurance reserve; 4096 prompt, 4096 newest, and at most 5120 older tokens. Position tensors, pointers, masks, score metadata, temporary tensors and model activations are additional; this is not a RAM cap.
validation: Two label-free score-capture-only seq3 replays must reproduce the raw-window masks and traces exactly. Two independent active engineering replays per strategy must preserve original selection and feature/position identity, exact budgets, model parameters, pointer trace and deterministic outputs. Independently verify receipts and mask hashes. Candidate execution remains disabled until independent engineering verification and the same-state utility diagnostic are completed. Seq23 requires inset exclusion before detection and video processing. Evaluate labels only after prediction. No efficacy claim from engineering checks.
limitations: Prompt errors contaminate all reference prototypes; apparent boundary appearance may represent illumination or folds. Fixed prototypes cannot follow changing appearance, and no learned channel attention is claimed. Protected conditioning and newest entries consume the same feature budget for every arm. Comparisons with historical ground-truth-prompt native/Lean runs are unequal-prompt references.
